title: Fuel Needed for Trip Calculator: Litres Required
description: Estimate how much fuel a journey needs from distance and L/100 km consumption with the Fuel Needed for Trip Calculator. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 1,200 km tour at 7.5 L/100 km needs exactly 90.0 litres — two ordinary tankfuls, planned before the mountains.
quick_answer: The Fuel Needed for Trip Calculator estimates a journey's fuel quantity from its distance in kilometres and your car's consumption in litres per 100 km. Enter both and read the litres required — the figure tank planning, remote routes and rental decisions are quietly built on.

faq: Is this exact?
The arithmetic is exact; the consumption is your estimate. Real journeys vary with terrain, weather and load — treat the result as the planned quantity and carry a margin.
What consumption format is used?
Litres per 100 km, the European standard. If you think in mpg, the Gallons Needed tool takes miles and mpg natively.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Consumption already absorbs your driving pattern if you enter your real figure; traffic is not a separate input.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind — and fuel is burned on the road figure. Enter road kilometres.
Can route results change over time?
Your car's consumption drifts with maintenance and season. Recheck it per tank and the estimates stay honest.
How much margin should I add?
Enough for a missed station and a detour — many planners add 10–15% or keep the tank above a quarter. The calculator gives the need; the margin is your judgement.
Does it give the cost too?
Quantity here; cost in the Fuel Cost Calculator, which multiplies by your price.
Tank smaller than the trip needs — how many fills?
Divide litres needed by usable tank capacity and round up: 90 L through a 45 L usable tank is two fills after the starting amount. The Fuel Stop Planner places them.
Does air conditioning really change it?
Measurably on small cars in hot weather — it is inside your real-world consumption if you measured it in summer. Use the season's figure for the season's trip.
Motorway versus mountain consumption?
Different by a wide margin in most cars. Enter the figure for the terrain the trip actually crosses — or price both halves separately and add.
